From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Cebuano

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Spanish distrito.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Hyphenation: dis‧tri‧to

Noun

[edit]

distrito

  1. a congressional district
  2. a district; a sector; a zone

Synonyms

[edit]
  • (a district): purok

Esperanto

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /disˈtrito/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ito
  • Syllabification: dis‧tri‧to

Noun

[edit]

distrito (accusative singular distriton, plural distritoj, accusative plural distritojn)

  1. singular past nominal passive participle of distri

Hiligaynon

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish distrito, from Latin districtus, from distringĕre.

Noun

[edit]

distríto

  1. territory, province, district

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin districtus, from distringō. Doublet of Detroit.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /d͡ʒisˈtɾi.tu/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /d͡ʒisˈtɾi.tu/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /d͡ʒiʃˈtɾi.tu/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /d͡ʒisˈtɾi.to/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /dɨʃˈtɾi.tu/, /diʃˈtɾi.tu/

  • Hyphenation: dis‧tri‧to

Noun

[edit]

distrito m (plural distritos)

  1. district

Derived terms

[edit]
  • distrital

Further reading

[edit]
  • “distrito”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “distrito”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

    Tagalog distrito

      Borrowed from Spanish distrito, a learned borrowing from Latin districtus, from distringō, from dis- + stringō.

      Pronunciation

      • Syllabification: dis‧tri‧to

      distrito (Baybayin spelling ᜇᜒᜐ᜔ᜆ᜔ᜇᜒᜆᜓ)

      1. district
        Synonym: purok
